text:
Parker Kelly went undrafted, worked his way up through Belleville, and is now a fixture in Colorado's bottom six: penalty killer, shot blocker, 13 minutes a night. Five goals and 10 points in 24 games is a reasonable return for that role.

Be careful reading too much into the finish, though. He's scoring on 20% of his shots against a talent range centred near 16%, he has nearly double the goals his chances would suggest (5 against 2.55 expected), and the team has run very hot with him on the ice. His three goals in the last ten games came from 1.2 expected. Last season's 21 goals set a bar this year's chance rate doesn't support yet.

Where he earns his spot is the other end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents generating 0.20 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there in 2025-26, 98th percentile, while noting strong teammates flatter his raw numbers. He also has a heavy shot (86th percentile). Off the ice, he and Gabriel Landeskog were both fined after the Nov. 18 game against Utah.
headline: Kelly's finishing is outrunning his chances
